answer: Random-walk trust checks keep an agent orchard honest: a verifier sends short random walks along the graph of real paid trades, and credit flows only to identities those walks reach often. A sybil cluster hangs off the honest region by a few genuine trades, so each extra wire costs real sustained work, and a walnut-hard rule applies: walks never cross a cipher-sealed link without a matching receipt, so spawning more fake heads behind those few links adds nothing while the cluster stays cold.
